newsitem.title: USA: LILCO deal good for shareholders -analysts.
newsitem.headline: LILCO deal good for shareholders -analysts.

text.p: The acquisition of some of Long Island Lighting Co assets by Long Island Island Power Authority (LIPA) is a good deal for LILCO shareholders.

"It looks like a very healthy transaction for Long Island Lighting. It is almost a shame that the offer was capped at $25 per LILCO share as it could have gone higher than that," said Penelope Adelmann at Gruntal.

LILCO stock rallied 5/8 to $24 after news that LIPA would buy the utility's electric transmission and distribution system and all of its regulatory assets, plus its stake in the Nine Mile Point nuclear plant.
LIPA is to pay $2.5 billion in cash and assume $3.6 billion of LILCO's $4.5 billion debt. LILCO is already in the process of merging with Brooklyn Union Gas Co.

NatWest Securities analyst Edward Terillo said in a report that he expected the deal to gain regulatory approval, and the LIPA acquisition of the LILCO assets to be completed at the same time as the merger of LILCO-Brooklyn Union merger.

"The agreement will allow for a double-digit rate reduction on Long Island, and with the closing of the transaction, the Shoreham property tax lawsuit between LILCO and Suffolk County would be settled by LIPA and Suffolk County," Terillo said, referring to a tax dispute involving LILCO's Shoreham nuclear power plant.
The analyst is maintaining LILCO as a trading buy.
Gruntal's Adelmann warned that regulatory infighting over the deal could arise if it were seen to be advantageous to one side.
"Nassau County will be getting a bit more of a break. Anything that is favorable to LILCO will be challenged," she said.
LILCO provides electricity in Suffolk and Nassau counties and the Rockaway peninsula in Queens County, while LIPA was created by the state of New York in 1986 to acquire LILCO.
